targets.full_source_formulation_normalized: For every inductively minimal finite pair (Gamma,G), the pair is RWPRI and has properties (2T)_1 and (IP)_2.
An inductively minimal pair of even rank is PRI.
For an inductively minimal pair, failure of PRI implies QPRI; failure of PRI occurs exactly when the connected diagram has a middle (a nonend whose deletion components have equal cardinality).
targets.interpretive_note: The printed phrase "this is the case" is read as failure of PRI, as its proof confirms. PRI pairs are also QPRI under the source definition. The manuscript states the stronger unambiguous profile. A middle explicitly requires at least two deletion components; the one-vertex diagram has none.

targets.full_source_formulation_normalized: An inductively minimal pair is RPRI if and only if its diagram is a complete graph.

For a normal subgroup N of G, mu(G) <= mu(G/N)+mu_prime(N). If N is abelian, mu(G) <= mu(G/N)+mu_prime_G(N), with G acting on N by conjugation. The printed source says a group; this contract takes finite G.

For n >= 7, every independent generating set S of S_n of size n-1 is S(T), the edge transpositions of a labelled tree T, or {s} union {(s t)^epsilon(t): t in S(T) except s}, where s in S(T) and epsilon(t) in {+1,-1}. Conversely every set of either form is an independent generating set of S_n.

For the two families of Theorem 2.1, the numbers of actual unordered generating sets are n^(n-2) and (n-1)n^(n-2), respectively; identifying each 3-cycle with its inverse changes the second count to binomial(n,2)(n-1)^(n-3). Degree n >= 7 is inherited from that theorem.
For n >= 7 every independent generating set (s_i:i in I) of S_n of size n-1 is strongly independent: with G_J=<s_i:i not in J>, G_J intersect G_K = G_(J union K) for all J,K subsets of I.
For n >= 7 and B <= S_n, mu(S_n,B)=n-1 implies B=1.

targets.full_source_formulation_normalized: A source coset geometry for G with Borel B has rank <= mu_prime(G,B). An RWPRI source coset geometry has rank <= mu(G,B), and choices s_i in H_(I minus {i}) outside H_i form a strongly independent relative generating family. The printed source does not impose finite G; this contract takes finite G.

For n >= 7 there is a bijection between independent generating sets of S_n of size n-1, modulo simultaneous conjugation and inversion of individual generators, and RWPRI coset geometries for S_n of rank n-1. The specified group action is retained and set order/type labels may be renamed.
For n >= 7 every source coset geometry of S_n of rank n-1 is RWPRI, without an initial RWPRI hypothesis.
For B<=G and Phi=Phi(G), a family (s_i) is an independent generating family of G relative to B iff (Phi s_i) is an independent generating family of G/Phi relative to BPhi/Phi.
A firm RWPRI coset geometry satisfies Phi(G)<=H_i for every type i, including infinite G.
If N is normal in G and N<=H_i for every type of a coset pregeometry, that pregeometry is isomorphic to the coset pregeometry (G/N,(H_i/N)).
A firm RWPRI coset geometry (G,(H_i)) is isomorphic to (G/Phi(G),(H_i/Phi(G))).
Every firm RWPRI geometry is isomorphic to a firm RWPRI geometry for a Frattini-free group.
A rank-two coset pregeometry (G,(H_1,H_2)) is a direct sum iff H_1 H_2=G.
For proper U,W<F_p^k with W not contained in U, if U is maximal and U intersect W is maximal in U, then W is maximal in F_p^k.
A firm coset geometry of a finite p-group is RWPRI iff it is RPRI.
A firm RWPRI coset geometry of a p-group is a direct sum of primitive rank-one geometries. The source section fixes finite p-groups, although this theorem sentence omits the word finite.
For every residue at a flag of type J, Phi(H_J)<=H_J intersect H_i for every remaining type i; this is necessary, not sufficient.

The largest normal subgroup of G contained in B is core_G(B)=intersection_i core_G(H_i); quotienting yields the faithful coset action, and for firm RWPRI geometries this kernel contains Phi(G). The separately cited Archer2004 classification at the end of this section is retained, not newly proved.
Construction, rank, firmness, residual connectedness, flag transitivity and thickness with the exact thin exception k=1,n=3.
Type-preserving automorphism group S_N and type-permuting group S_N times S_r.
Complete diagram, type size binom(N,k), corrected panel order binom(n-k,k)-1, diameter 2 ceil(k/(n-2k))+1 and gonality 3 for n=2k+1, 2 otherwise.
Incidence graph KG(N,k) tensor K_r, locally KG(N-k,k) tensor K_(r-1).
S_N is transitive on maximal cliques.
The geometric rank-two intersection property holds exactly when n=2k+1.
The 63-vertex graph for k=2,n=5,r=3 is locally Desargues and its full uncolored graph automorphism group is S_7 times S_3, not S_7.

U.Coset.statement_exact_markdown:
**Proposition U.Coset (exact coset transport).** Let \((H_i)_{i\in I}\) be subgroups of \(G\), let \(B=\bigcap_i H_i\), and let \(N\unlhd G\) satisfy \(N\leq B\). Quotienting by \(N\) gives a bijection
\[
H_i g\longmapsto (H_i/N)(gN)
\tag{1.5}
\]
on the typed right cosets. It preserves the intersections of arbitrary families of those cosets, including the existence of a common element. It consequently preserves incidence, flags, residues and all properties determined by the resulting incidence system. The actions of \(G\) and \(G/N\) have the same permutation image. Maximality of any inclusion between intersections of the \(H_i\) is preserved.

formal_coverage.gap: Written proof; no whole-theorem certificate asserted.

U.RelativeBound.statement_exact_markdown:
**Proposition U.RelativeBound (normal quotient bound).** If \(G\) is finite and \(N\unlhd G\), then
\[
m(G)\leq m(G/N)+i(N).
\tag{6.1}
\]
If \(N\) is abelian, then \(i(N)\) can be replaced by \(i_G(N)\).

formal_coverage.gap: Written proof; no whole-theorem certificate asserted.

U.Relative.statement_exact_markdown:
**Theorem U.Relative (generation from residual maximality).** Suppose all \(H_J\), \(J\subseteq I\), are distinct, and for every \(J\subsetneq I\) there is \(k\notin J\) such that \(H_{J\cup\{k\}}\) is maximal in \(H_J\). Choose
\[
s_i\in H_{I\setminus\{i\}}\setminus H_i.
\tag{6.2}
\]
Then
\[
H_J=\langle B,s_i:i\notin J\rangle\quad(J\subseteq I).
\tag{6.3}
\]
In particular these elements generate \(G\) irredundantly relative to \(B\), and their relative parabolics satisfy
\[
\langle B,s_i:i\in S\rangle\cap\langle B,s_i:i\in T\rangle
=\langle B,s_i:i\in S\cap T\rangle.
\tag{6.4}
\]
The group need not be finite.

formal_coverage.gap: Written proof; no whole-theorem certificate asserted.

U.Maximal.statement_exact_markdown: **Lemma U.Maximal (relative finite generation).** If \(G=\langle B,t_1,\ldots,t_r\rangle\) with \(r\) finite, then every proper subgroup containing \(B\) is contained in a maximal subgroup of \(G\).

formal_coverage.gap: Written proof; no whole-theorem certificate asserted.

U.FrattiniTransport.statement_exact_markdown: **Theorem U.FrattiniTransport (relative generating families).** Under the maximal-overgroup hypothesis of (6.5), a finite indexed family is an irredundant relative generating family of \(G\) over \(B\) if and only if its image is one of \(G/\Phi(G)\) over \(B\Phi(G)/\Phi(G)\).

formal_coverage.gap: Written proof; no whole-theorem certificate asserted.

U.FrattiniLadder.statement_exact_markdown:
**Theorem U.FrattiniLadder (containment in the common stabilizer).** Suppose the \(H_J\) are all distinct and some ordering of \(I=\{1,\ldots,r\}\) gives a chain
\[
G=K_0>K_1>\cdots>K_r=B,\qquad K_j=H_{\{1,\ldots,j\}},
\tag{6.6}
\]
in which every inclusion is maximal. If \(N\unlhd G\) lies in every maximal subgroup of \(G\), then \(N\leq B\).

formal_coverage.gap: Written proof; no whole-theorem certificate asserted.
